newsitem.title: CHINA: Rainstorms break record in Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Rainstorms break record in Hong Kong.

text.p: Torrential rain that soaked Hong Kong on its return to China on July 1, and which has continued almost daily since, was the heaviest since records began in 1884, the Hong Kong Observatory said.

Heavy rainstorms, which have lashed the territory since late June, caused flooding in rural areas of the northern New Territories on Saturday, where entire villages were awash in knee-deep murky waters.
The almost incessant rain between July 1 and 18 is the heaviest on record compared to similar periods in any July since Hong Kong began observations in 1884, the observatory said.

Millions of television viewers around the world watched British heir to the throne Prince Charles get soaked as he delivered a speech on the eve of the territory's handover. Between then and July 18, a total 679 mm of rain was recorded, breaking the previous record of 641.5 mm during the same period in 1886.

"With the trough of low pressure staying near the south China coast, the weather is expected to remain unsettled. For the next couple of days, it will be cloudy with rain at times," the observatory said.
Part of a flat in a densely populated area on Hong Kong island collapsed on Saturday, injuring a 66-year-old woman and four other passers-by.
A government spokesman said it was unclear if dampness caused the collapse and investigations were continuing.
The injured woman was in stable condition in hospital. The others escaped with minor injuries.
